B1.title: B1 · What was changed?
B1.description: A class placed equal-sized pieces of potato tissue in five sucrose solutions. They measured the mean percentage change in mass after 20 minutes. Which statement correctly identifies the independent variable and explains why?

choices.text: Sucrose concentration, because the class deliberately changed it between treatment groups.
Percentage change in mass, because it was the outcome recorded after treatment.
Time in solution, because it must increase whenever concentration increases.
The original potato mass, because all measured quantities are independent variables.

B2.title: B2 · Build a fair comparison
B2.description: Select all procedures that help isolate the effect of sucrose concentration. The outcome is percentage mass change. Choose only procedures that strengthen this comparison; incorrect selections reduce credit.

choices.text: Use pieces cut to the same dimensions from the same potato variety and batch.
Keep immersion time, temperature, solution volume, and blotting method the same.
Randomly assign pieces to concentrations and test several pieces at each concentration.
Leave pieces in stronger solutions longer so their changes are easier to see.
Remove any piece whose result disagrees with the prediction, without checking for a procedural error.

B3.title: B3 · Connect the calculation to water movement
B3.description:
One piece increased from 10.0 g to 10.8 g. Percentage change = (final mass − initial mass) ÷ initial mass × 100.
Its percentage change was {{percent}} %. Enter the number without the % sign.
Assuming the mass change was due to water movement, the net movement of water was {{direction}} the potato cells. Enter "into" or "out of".

B4.title: B4 · Evaluate an explanation of zero change
B4.description:
The graph shows mean mass changes of +12%, +8%, +4%, 0%, and −4% at sucrose concentrations of 0.00, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, and 0.40 mol/L, respectively. There were five pieces at each concentration.
A student says: "At 0.30 mol/L, water molecules stopped moving, and this proves that every potato cell contains exactly 0.30 mol/L sucrose."
In 3–4 sentences, identify two problems with that explanation. Use the graph to give a better explanation of the zero mean mass change. Distinguish net movement from movement of individual molecules.

rubric.expected_answer:
Reference: At about 0.30 mol/L, the mean mass change is zero, suggesting approximately balanced inward and outward water movement under these conditions. Individual water molecules continue moving; zero net movement is dynamic balance, not stopped motion. A mean of zero does not establish that every piece or cell behaved identically. Potato cells contain a mixture of solutes, so the external sucrose concentration does not identify an exact internal sucrose concentration for every cell.
Rubric (6): 1 for citing 0.30 mol/L and zero mean change; 2 for continued movement in both directions with approximately balanced rates; 2 for explaining why the exact-sucrose/every-cell claim is unsupported (mixture of solutes, average versus individuals, or biological variation; one well-explained reason suffices); 1 for a coherent qualified interpretation. A concentration or the phrase "no net movement" alone earns at most 1. Do not require terminology beyond Grade 10.

B5.title: B5 · Predict, then design a check
B5.description:
The same class now proposes a 0.50 mol/L sucrose solution. The original mean changes were +12%, +8%, +4%, 0%, and −4% at 0.00, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, and 0.40 mol/L. Assume intact cell membranes and the same 20-minute procedure.
In 3–4 sentences: predict whether the new mean mass change will be positive, near zero, or negative; explain the water movement; give one reason the original graph cannot guarantee an exact numerical change; and describe a fair test of your prediction.

rubric.expected_answer:
Reference: Predict a negative change because the more concentrated external solution should produce net movement of water out of the cells. The 0.50 mol/L treatment is outside the measured range: extrapolation may not stay linear, and biological variation matters. Test multiple randomly assigned, similar-sized pieces at 0.50 mol/L alongside a repeated measured comparison such as 0.40 mol/L, holding time, temperature, potato source, solution volume, and blotting method constant; compare mean percentage changes.
Rubric (6): 1 negative prediction; 1 outward water movement with concentration reasoning; 1 explicit uncertainty about extrapolating or assuming linearity; 1 replicated new treatment and a comparison treatment; 1 at least two appropriate held-constant variables; 1 measure and compare mean percentage mass changes. An estimate of −8% may be included only as a tentative linear extrapolation, not an established fact. A bare prediction earns at most 1.

G1.title: G1 · Match sides using angle evidence
G1.description:
In triangles ABC and DEF, angle A and angle D are right angles, and angle B equals angle E. Thus A ↔ D, B ↔ E, and C ↔ F. AB = 4 cm, AC = 3 cm, BC = 5 cm, DE = 6 cm, and DF = 4.5 cm.
Which pairing and explanation correctly identifies the side corresponding to BC?

choices.text: BC corresponds to DE because DE is drawn horizontally.
BC corresponds to EF because endpoints B and C correspond to E and F.
BC corresponds to DF because both names end with the last letter of a triangle.
BC cannot have a corresponding side unless both triangles have equal areas.

G2.title: G2 · Use one consistent scale factor
G2.description:
Triangles ABC and DEF are similar with A ↔ D, B ↔ E, C ↔ F. AB = 4 cm, DE = 6 cm, and BC = 5 cm.
The enlargement factor from ABC to DEF is {{factor}}.
Using that same factor, EF is {{length}} cm.
Enter terminating decimals (for example, 2.5), without units.

G3.title: G3 · Decide which evidence is sufficient
G3.description: Consider any two nondegenerate triangles. Select every statement that is sufficient to prove they are similar. Each statement is a separate scenario; do not combine evidence from different choices. Incorrect selections reduce credit.

choices.text: Two pairs of corresponding angles are equal.
All three pairs of corresponding side lengths have the same ratio.
One pair of corresponding angles is equal.
One side of the second triangle is twice one side of the first triangle.
Both triangles have the same perimeter.

G4.title: G4 · Repair an area-scaling argument
G4.description:
An original triangular sign has area 12 cm². A designer makes a similar sign with every side length three times as large. A draft solution says: "The new area is 36 cm² because I multiplied by 3."
In 2–3 sentences, explain the error using base and height (or a decomposition argument), calculate the correct area, and explain why the units are square centimeters.

rubric.expected_answer:
Reference: Both the base and its corresponding perpendicular height scale by 3, so (1/2)(3b)(3h) = 9(1/2 bh). The area becomes 9 × 12 = 108 cm². Area measures two-dimensional coverage, so its units are squared.
Rubric (6): 1 identifies confusing a length scale with an area scale; 2 explains both independent dimensions scaling by 3 (or equivalent nine-copy decomposition); 1 obtains area factor 9; 1 obtains 108; 1 explains cm² as two-dimensional coverage. A bare "108 cm²" earns 1; an answer with the correct formula and explanatory substitutions can earn full credit without extra prose.

G5.title: G5 · Test a right angle with slopes
G5.description: The coordinate diagram has A(0, 0), B(4, 2), C(3, 4), and D(−1, 2), joined in that order. Which argument establishes that AB and BC are perpendicular?

choices.text: Their slopes are 1/2 and −2; the product is −1.
Their slopes are 1/2 and 2; any two positive slopes make a right angle.
Their slopes are 2 and −2; opposite slopes always make a right angle.
Their slopes are equal because both segments touch B.

G6.title: G6 · Locate a diagonal midpoint
G6.description:
For A(0, 0) and C(3, 4), find the midpoint M of diagonal AC. Use the midpoint rule, which averages the endpoint coordinates.
M = ({{xcoord}}, {{ycoord}}).
Enter terminating decimals or whole numbers, without units.

G7.title: G7 · Separate rectangle facts from square facts
G7.description: Use A(0, 0), B(4, 2), C(3, 4), and D(−1, 2). Select every true statement about this quadrilateral. Use coordinates or geometric reasoning, not its appearance. Incorrect selections reduce credit.

choices.text: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
All four side lengths are equal.
The diagonals AC and BD have equal lengths.
The diagonals AC and BD are perpendicular.
It must be a square because it has a right angle.

G8.title: G8 · Verify an area in two ways
G8.description:
A library floor fits inside a 12 m by 8 m rectangle. A 4 m-wide by 3 m-deep rectangular service area is excluded from the upper-right corner. All corners are right angles.
Show two different area calculations that agree: (1) subtract the excluded area from the outer rectangle; (2) split the usable L-shaped region into two nonoverlapping rectangles. State the usable floor area and explain why your two rectangles neither overlap nor leave a gap.

rubric.expected_answer:
Reference: Outer-minus-cutout: 12 × 8 − 4 × 3 = 96 − 12 = 84 m². A horizontal split gives a 12 × 5 lower rectangle and an 8 × 3 upper-left rectangle: 60 + 24 = 84 m². Alternatively, an 8 × 8 left rectangle plus a 4 × 5 lower-right rectangle gives 64 + 20 = 84 m². The rectangles share only an edge and together fill precisely the usable region.
Rubric (6): 2 correct subtraction setup and result; 2 a correct nonoverlapping two-rectangle setup and sum (award 1 if a minor arithmetic slip follows correct dimensions); 1 explains complete coverage without overlap; 1 states 84 m² with units. A bare correct final area earns only 1. Give follow-through credit for a consistent minor arithmetic error; do not award the same final-result point twice.

G9.title: G9 · Distinguish sector area from arc length
G9.description: A circular reading rug has radius 6 ft. A 90° sector is reserved for a display. Which expression correctly gives the AREA of that sector and explains the fraction used?

choices.text: 3π ft², because a quarter of the circumference gives sector area.
36π ft², because the sector uses the circle’s full radius.
9π ft², because 90/360 = 1/4 and one quarter of π × 6² is 9π.
18π ft², because every sector is half a circle.

G10.title: G10 · Adapt the design to a new constraint
G10.description:
Return to the library’s 12 m by 8 m outer rectangle. The service area must remain in the upper-right corner and 3 m deep, but its width may change. At least 80 m² must remain usable.
A designer proposes increasing the service-area width from 4 m to 6 m. In a short calculation and 2–3 sentences:
• Test whether 6 m meets the usable-area requirement.
• Find the greatest mathematically allowed width (an exact fraction is acceptable).
• Recommend the greatest allowed WHOLE-METER width, and check its usable area.
Explain why a smaller service area leaves more usable floor.

rubric.expected_answer:
Reference: Usable area U = 12 × 8 − 3w = 96 − 3w. At w = 6, U = 78 m², so the proposal fails the 80 m² minimum. Solving 96 − 3w ≥ 80 gives 3w ≤ 16, hence w ≤ 16/3 m (5 1/3 m). The greatest whole-meter choice is 5 m; its usable area is 96 − 15 = 81 m², which meets the constraint. A narrower excluded strip removes less area. The picture shows the original 4 m width, not the changed proposal.
Rubric (8): 2 obtains 78 m² and rejects the 6 m proposal; 2 states and correctly solves the inequality to 16/3 m (allow 5.33 m as a conservative rounded value with clear reasoning; do not treat 5.34 as an allowed bound); 1 recommends 5 m as the greatest whole-meter width; 1 checks 81 m² ≥ 80 m²; 1 explains the inverse width-versus-usable-area relationship; 1 presents a coherent recommendation separating original, proposed, and chosen dimensions. A list of final numbers without reasoning earns at most 3. Accept equivalent reasoning without algebraic inequality notation.

essay_topic.question:
## Books or a creative media space?
**English argument writing · Suggested time: 15 minutes · Target: 200–300 words**

Riverton High School has a one-time $6,000 library improvement grant. It can choose ONE of the two complete plans below this year. Write an argument recommending a plan to the school council. There is no predetermined correct choice.

### Source A — Librarian’s proposal (fictional)
Many students request books that are unavailable or have long waiting lists. A books plan would add current fiction, practical nonfiction, and books in several languages. Books can be borrowed for use at home without an internet connection. They still need shelving and occasional replacement. A creative space would be useful, but its limited seats could make access difficult during busy periods.

### Source B — Student media club’s proposal (fictional)
A small media space could let students record podcasts, edit video, and work on presentations even if they lack equipment at home. Students could learn from each other across subjects. The proposed space has only six seats and requires supervised booking. Club members support scheduled access for all students, not priority for their club. Some students would still prefer a quiet place to read.

### Source C — Planning table (fictional estimates, not research findings)
| Measure | Books plan | Creative media plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One-time grant cost | $6,000 | $6,000 |
| What is added | 300 print books | 6-seat recording/editing space |
| Access outside school | Books may be borrowed | Equipment stays at school |
| Main ongoing need | Shelving and replacements | Supervision and maintenance |
| First-choice votes in a voluntary student poll | 72 | 48 |

The poll had 120 respondents out of 600 students. It was voluntary, and students selected only one plan. The votes do not establish what every student wants or how much either plan would improve learning.

### Your task
State a clear claim. Use specific evidence from at least TWO labeled sources and explain how it supports your recommendation. Address a reasonable counterargument, identify a limitation or uncertainty in the evidence, and end with a justified conclusion. Do not invent outside statistics or quotations. Refer to sources as A, B, or C; formal citations are unnecessary.

You may use the available AI assistant for help. Decide what to accept, check the packet yourself, and submit reasoning you can explain. Do not include personal information. If AI suggests a fact absent from the packet, do not treat it as supplied evidence.

### Assessment guide
A reviewer will look for: (1) a focused claim and logical organization; (2) accurate evidence from two sources with an explanation of each; (3) a fair counterargument and a meaningful response; (4) recognition of an evidence limitation; and (5) a clear conclusion and readable prose. Either plan can earn strong feedback. This essay is reviewed by a person, not automatically scored by the platform. The word target is advisory.

B5.rationale: Synthetic rubric review: negative prediction: 1 point(s); outward water movement: 1 point(s); extrapolation uncertainty: 1 point(s); replication and comparison: 1 point(s); controlled variables: 1 point(s); mean percentage changes: 1 point(s). Credit is limited to the reasoning stated in the submitted answer.

G8.text: Subtracting gives 12 × 8 − 4 × 3 = 84 m². Splitting gives a 12 × 5 bottom rectangle and an 8 × 3 top-left rectangle, or 60 + 24 = 84 m². They share a boundary but no area, and together cover the entire L.

chats.assistant: The excluded area is 3 × 6 = 18 m², leaving 78 m², which fails. Solve 96 − 3w ≥ 80 to get w ≤ 16/3. The greatest whole-meter width is 5 m, leaving 81 m².

chats.question: G4
chats.user: I multiplied the original 12 cm² by three, but the sign is enlarged in every length. What have I missed?
chats.assistant: Both base and perpendicular height triple. The area factor is 3 × 3 = 9, so 12 × 9 = 108 cm². Squared units describe coverage in two dimensions.

chats.question: G2
chats.user: AB is four, DE is six and BC is five. I think the enlargement factor is 1.5. How do I use the correspondence?
chats.assistant: The factor from ABC to DEF is 6/4 = 1.5. Since B corresponds to E and C to F, BC corresponds to EF, so EF = 5 × 1.5 = 7.5 cm.

chats.question: G3
chats.user: I recognize equal corresponding angles. Is one equal angle enough to say two triangles are similar?
chats.assistant: One equal angle alone is insufficient. Two pairs of equal angles establish AA similarity, or all three corresponding side pairs can have the same ratio. Equal perimeter alone is not enough.

chats.question: G7
chats.user: ABCD has a right angle. I am tempted to call it a square. Which coordinate check would distinguish a square from a rectangle?
chats.assistant: Compare adjacent side lengths: AB has length √20 and BC has length √5. They differ, so this rectangle is not a square. Its opposite sides are parallel and its diagonals have equal lengths.
